literal: what is digested having known, having adhered firmly, contrary things that are not, let one eat, completely having hungered.
translation: Knowing that the previous meal has been digested and firmly adhering to that rule, let one eat foods that are not contrary to health, only after getting completely hungry.
modern: முன்பு உண்ட உணவு செரித்ததை அறிந்து, அந்த முறையை உறுதியாகப் பின்பற்றி, உடலுக்கு மாறுபடாத உணவுகளை நன்கு பசித்த பிறகு உண்ண வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the fundamental rules for a healthy diet. The word 'அற்றது' (what is digested) emphasizes that one must wait until the previous meal is fully processed by the body. 'கடைப்பிடித்து' (adhering firmly) stresses the importance of making this a strict, unwavering habit. Finally, 'மாறு அல்ல' (things that are not contrary) and 'துவரப் பசித்து' (having hungered completely) advise eating only agreeable foods and only when true hunger sets in, ensuring optimal health.
